subtitle: Three commits after the last deploy: the amount parsing change, the adjustments file for the report, and a finance note. Every hunk read.

verdict.text: Request changes. Commit 49bc16d drops the decimal comma from `parse_amount` and deletes the only test that covered it, so the first export with `12,50` stops the whole import; the new `read_adjustments` repeats the same parsing. Restore the comma handling and its test, and give the adjustments file the same parser and a test, then this can merge. [high]

sections.title: Findings
sections.intro: Ordered by what reaches a user or the data once merged. Each was read in the diff and the code around it; the tests named in each fix are written out under *Changed code without a test*.

items.title: A decimal comma now stops the whole import
items.evidence: Before: `Decimal(value.strip().replace(",", "."))`. After: `Decimal(value.strip())`. The same commit deletes `test_decimal_comma`, which fed `12,50` and expected `12.50`. `read_orders` calls `parse_amount` for every line and nothing catches `InvalidOperation`, so one such row ends `import_file` before the first `save_order` (importer.py:58, storage.py:27). [high]
items.fix: Keep the comma: `Decimal(value.strip().replace(",", "."))`, or refuse the row with its line number and go on. Restore the test.

items.title: `read_adjustments` has the same parsing
items.evidence: `Decimal(row["amount"].strip())` on a file finance edits by hand, with `;` as the separator, the same convention as the order export. A comma in `amount` raises inside `daily_report` and the report is not written. [high]
items.fix: One `parse_amount` for both files, in `importer.py`, used by `report.py`.

items.title: A test was deleted with no reason in the diff
items.evidence: `ParseAmountTest.test_decimal_comma` is removed; the commit message says *simplify*, not *drop decimal commas*. A test deleted without a reason is a behaviour removed without a decision. [high]
items.fix: Restore it; if the comma is meant to go, say so in the commit and in README.

items.title: `read_adjustments` and `--adjustments` have no test
items.evidence: The facts list both source files under *source without test change*; `tests/` has no test of `report.py` at all. [high]
items.fix: The two tests written out below.

items.title: `open(path)` of a path from a parameter
items.evidence: Rule hit `path-from-input`: the path comes from the `--adjustments` argument. It is given by the operator on the command line, not by a request, and the process already reads any file the operator names. [high]
items.reason: An operator's own command-line path is not untrusted input for this program; there is no root to confine it to.

blocks.code:
import tempfile
import unittest
from decimal import Decimal

from acme_orders import report


class AdjustmentsTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def _file(self, amount):
        f = tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile("w", suffix=".csv", delete=False, encoding="utf-8")
        f.write("note;amount\nrefund;" + amount + "\n")
        f.close()
        return f.name

    def test_dot(self):
        self.assertEqual(report.read_adjustments(self._file("12.50")), Decimal("12.50"))

    def test_comma_like_the_order_export(self):
        self.assertEqual(report.read_adjustments(self._file("12,50")), Decimal("12.50"))

    def test_report_shows_the_adjustments(self):
        html = report.daily_report([], "2026-10-01", self._file("3.00"))
        self.assertIn("Adjustments: 3.00", html)
